subject: Mathematics

source.topic: Numbers, operations and relationships: Context-free calculations to 99
source.subtopic: Multiply numbers 1 to 10 by 2 and 5 (weeks 1-2), 2 and 4 (weeks 3-4), 5 and 3 (weeks 5-6), 3 and 5 (weeks 7-8), 3 and 4 (weeks 9-10)

show.line: Four tricycles. Each has three wheels. Three, six, nine, twelve. Four times three equals twelve!

rounds.prompt: Two clovers. Three leaves on each. Count the leaves in threes. How many?
rounds.praise: Six leaves! Two times three is six.

rounds.prompt: Five triangles. Three sides each. Count the sides in threes. How many sides?
rounds.praise: Fifteen! Five times three is fifteen.

rounds.prompt: Three times three. Three groups of three. Say the answer.
Six times three. What is the answer?
rounds.praise: Eighteen! Three, six, nine, twelve, fifteen, eighteen.

rounds.story: Each bag has three oranges. Gogo buys seven bags. How many oranges does she buy?

rounds.prompt: Count in threes. Three, six, nine, twelve. What comes next?
Which picture shows four times three?
rounds.praise: Yes! Four groups with three in each.

hints: Count in threes, once for each group. Three, six, nine.
Times means groups of. Four times three is four groups of three.

beat_the_tutor.tutor_try: Three, six, nine, twelve. Five times three is twelve!
beat_the_tutor.win_line: You caught me! I only counted four threes. Three, six, nine, twelve, fifteen.
beat_the_tutor.gentle_line: Let's count five threes together. Three, six, nine, twelve, fifteen!

parent_line: Can work out groups of three up to 10 groups.
